Package org.geysermc.paletter

Class Paletter

java.lang.Object
org.geysermc.paletter.Paletter
public final class Paletter extends Object
Entry point: vanilla Bedrock data for every supported version, and the palettes compiled from it. 

 Paletter paletter = Paletter.bundled();
 PaletteLayer layer = PaletteLayer.builder("server")...build();

 // Once per client version, shared by all sessions on it
 Palette palette = paletter.palette(codec, BlockNetworkIds.HASHED, layer);
 // Optionally per session, sharing everything it does not change
 Palette sessionPalette = palette.extend(sessionLayer);
Everything is loaded lazily and cached; instances are thread safe. Block states and item components that are equal across versions are the same instances.

Canonical ids (canonicalBlocks(), canonicalItems()) are defined by the newest version, and valid in every palette of this instance.

Since:
1.0.0

    • block

      public @Nullable BedrockBlockState block(@NonNull org.cloudburstmc.nbt.NbtMap state)
      Parameters:
      state - a block state of any bundled version as {name, states}; extra keys are ignored. A state the newest version lacks is mapped forward to its newest equivalent (renamed identifiers, state keys added, removed or reset)
      Returns:
      its handle, or null if the newest version has no equivalent (see explainUnknown(NbtMap)). Custom blocks have handles of their own (BedrockBlockType.of(customBlock)), valid in palettes with their layer, see Palette.block(NbtMap)
      Since:
      1.0.0

    • blockOf

      public @Nullable BedrockBlockState blockOf(@NonNull BedrockItemVariant variant)
      The block state an item places, version independent: the block the newest version sends the item with (Palette.blockOf(org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockItemVariant)). Accepts variants of any bundled version like item(String, int). Vanilla variants of the newest data only; for a palette's view (fallbacks, custom content) use Palette.blockKeyOf(org.geysermc.paletter.vanilla.BedrockItemVariant).
      Returns:
      the block state, or null if the item is not a block item or has no handle
      Since:
      1.0.0
